title: Lax and oplax monoidal structures transferred by adjunction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories (categories with a tensor bifunctor, tensor unit, associator and left and right unitors satisfying the pentagon and triangle identities), with tensor units $\mathbf1_{\mathcal C},\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$, and let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ have an adjunction $L\dashv R$, with natural bijections $\Phi_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}(LX,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(X,RY)$. Use the lax/strong monoidal conventions of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport]. A lax monoidal structure means maps $\varepsilon_R:\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}\to R\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$ and $\mu_{Y,Z}:RY\otimes RZ\to R(Y\otimes Z)$ satisfying naturality and the associativity and unit coherence diagrams. An oplax monoidal structure has maps in the reverse directions and the corresponding coherence diagrams.

There is a bijection between lax monoidal structures on $R$ and oplax monoidal structures on $L$, obtained by adjunction mates. In the direction from $R$ to $L$, the oplax unit map is $\eta_L=\Phi_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C},\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}^{-1}(\varepsilon_R)$. In the reverse direction the lax unit map is $\varepsilon_R=\Phi_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C},\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}}(\eta_L)$. In particular, a strong monoidal left adjoint has a canonically lax monoidal right adjoint.

Its forward and inverse constructions are leftAdjointOplaxMonoidal at line 1064 (unit = homEquiv.symm of the lax unit, line 1065) and rightAdjointLaxMonoidal at line 947 (unit = homEquiv of the oplax unit, line 948).
